## Goal
`read_password` (`setup_config.py:169-186`) reads a password file with `read_text(encoding="utf-8")` and takes the first line stripped. A file saved by Windows Notepad usually starts with a UTF-8 byte order mark, so the "password" starts with an invisible character and the mailbox login fails with a message that points at the provider, not at the file. Read with `utf-8-sig`, strip a trailing CR and spaces (already done by `.strip()`), and report a file that is not valid text in plain words instead of an exception. Also make `_resolve` (`setup_config.py:164-166`) accept the forms Windows people paste: surrounding straight or curly double quotes (Explorer's "Copy as path"), `%USERPROFILE%`-style variables, and a trailing space, in addition to `~`. Behaviour for ordinary POSIX paths is unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. A password file with BOM + `secret\r\n` returns `secret` (write bytes `b"\xef\xbb\xbfsecret\r\n"` under `tmp_path`).
2. A file with no BOM, LF endings or no final newline returns the same text as before.
3. A file with only a BOM or only whitespace raises `SetupFileError` "the file is empty" (existing text).
4. A file with invalid UTF-8 bytes raises `SetupFileError` with a plain message that names the option (`mailbox.password_file`) and contains no bytes from the file.
5. `_resolve(base, '"C:\\Users\\x\\p.txt"')` (and the same with curly quotes) strips the quotes; `_resolve(base, "%MYVAR%/p.txt")` expands the variable when it is set (monkeypatch env) and leaves it as is when not; `~` still expands; relative paths still join `base`.
6. The password text never appears in any error message or log (sentinel check).
7. The YAML file itself with a BOM and CRLF endings still loads (`load`, `setup_config.py:144-161`): add the test; if it already passes, say so in VENDOR_STATUS.md.
8. WO-501..503 tests and the existing setup tests pass unchanged.
